title: 2.2 The Derivative as a Function; Differentiability

icans: I can find the derivative function f′(x) using the definition.
I can connect the graph of f to the graph of f′.
I can decide whether a function is differentiable at a number and explain why not.

vocab: a tangent line x = c where the slopes of f ___________ ∞ or −∞

blocks.p: y = x²: estimate the slope of the tangent line at each x.

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Derivative function: f′(x) = the limit as h → 0 of _______________

blocks.stem: Use the definition to find f′(x) for f(x) = x² − 3x.
Find f′(x) for f(x) = √x and the domain of f′.

notes: Graphs: f′ is positive where f is increasing, negative where f is decreasing, and _______________ where f has a horizontal tangent line.

blocks.stem: f(x) = x² − 4x. Find f′(x). Where is f′ negative, zero, and positive? What does that say about f?

notes: Differentiable means continuous: if f is differentiable at c, then f is _______________ at c.

blocks.stem: f(x) = x² if x ≤ 1;  2x − 1 if x > 1. Is f differentiable at 1?

notes: Not differentiable at corners, cusps, vertical tangent lines, and _______________.

blocks.stem:
Where is each function not differentiable, and why?
a.  f(x) = |x − 2|
b.  g(x) = ∛x
g(x) = 1 − 2x if x ≤ 1;  x − 2 if x > 1. Is g continuous at 1? Differentiable at 1?

(AP® Practice) f(x) = |x|. Which of the following are true?
I. f is continuous at 0.   II. f is differentiable at 0.   III. f(0) = 0.
(A) I only   (B) III only   (C) I and III only   (D) I, II, and III
